verses.83:2: Como são {dilecta} as vossas tendas, Senhor {virtutum}: * a minha alma anseia e desfalece {inatria} do Senhor.
verses.83:3: O meu coração e a minha carne * exultaram {indeum} Deus vivo.
verses.83:4: Pois o pardal encontrou para si uma casa: * e a rola {sibi2}, onde ponha os seus {pullos}.
verses.83:4b: {altaria}, Senhor {virtutum}: * meu Rei e meu Deus.
verses.83:5: Bem-aventurados os que habitam na vossa casa, Senhor: * pelos séculos dos séculos vos louvarão.
verses.83:6: Bem-aventurado o homem cujo auxílio {abste}: * dispôs no seu coração {ascensiones}, no vale de lágrimas, no lugar {posuit}.
verses.83:8: Pois o legislador dará a bênção, irão {devirtute}: * {videbitur} o Deus dos deuses em Sião.
verses.83:9: Senhor, Deus {virtutum}, escutai a minha oração: * dai ouvidos, Deus de Jacó.
verses.83:10: {v10a}: * e {respice} a face do vosso Cristo:
verses.83:11: Porque é melhor {diesuna} nos vossos átrios * do que milhares.
verses.83:11b: Escolhi ser {abjectus} na casa do meu Deus: * {magisquam} habitar nas tendas dos pecadores.
verses.83:12: Porque Deus ama a misericórdia e a verdade: * o Senhor dará a graça e a glória.
verses.83:13: Não privará {bonis} os que andam na inocência: * Senhor {virtutum}, bem-aventurado o homem que espera em vós.

decisions.why: dilécta is the participle 'beloved' (Greek ἀγαπητά); the glossary row diléctus → amado (59:7 *os vossos amados*). MS1932 and DRB say 'lovely' (*amáveis*), the familiar line; but *amável* in Brazil today is said of kind people, and of a place it sounds literary. *Amadas* is the Latin's word and the row's; it leaves open by whom they are loved, as the Latin does.

options.label: amadas
options.note: Ruling: the participle, as the diléctus row.

options.label: amáveis
options.note: MS1932 *Quão amáveis*, DRB 'lovely' — the familiar wording; 'worthy of love' rather than 'loved'.

decisions.why: D43 settles *Dóminus virtútum → o Senhor dos poderes* and flags it for Gustavo: MS1932 and DRB have *dos exércitos* (the Hebrew's Sabaoth); the Latin's *virtútes* (δυνάμεις) are powers. Four places in this psalm, one touch changes all four. Note 83:8 *de virtúte in virtútem*, decided apart (decision `devirtute`).

options.label: dos exércitos
options.note: MS1932, DRB 'hosts'; the Hebrew's reading, the name Brazilian ears know.

options.label: das virtudes
options.note: The cognate; would echo 83:8 *de virtude em virtude*; *virtude* is a moral quality to most ears.

decisions.latin: concupíscit, et déficit ánima mea in átria Dómini
decisions.why: *in átria* (accusative, εἰς τὰς αὐλάς) is what both verbs reach for. The glossary proposes *defícere in → desfalecer à espera de* (118:81), because bare *por* was heard as cause once (118:82 *pelo que dissestes*); it names 83:2 as the same build. Here *por* follows *anseia* (the concupíscere row's *ansiar por*), where it can only be the object of longing, and *à espera dos átrios* would make the soul wait for a place. Subject moved first (natural order, D2).

options.label: pelos átrios
options.note: Ruling: *ansiar por*, one preposition for both verbs, as the Latin has one.

decisions.why: *in* + accusative (ἐπὶ θεὸν ζῶντα): the joy is turned towards God. Portuguese *exultar* takes *em* (D44, *exultar em*); *para* (the open row *exsultáre* + dative) keeps the motion but is stiff. MS1932 *regozijam-se no Deus vivo*.
The Latin says *sibi* twice (*invénit sibi domum … nidum sibi*), as the Greek does (ἑαυτῷ … ἑαυτῇ). Kept (repetitions stay, D2). Dropping the second makes the colon two syllables shorter.

options.label: um ninho
options.note: *e a rola um ninho, onde ponha …* — lighter; loses the Latin's second *sibi*.

decisions.why: *pullus* is a young animal, a chick (L&S). *Filhotes* is the plain Brazilian word for young birds; MS1932's *filhinhos* is tender but a diminutive the Latin does not have.

decisions.latin: Altária tua, Dómine virtútum: Rex meus, et Deus meus.
decisions.why: The Latin verse has no verb. *Altária* can be read as an accusative in apposition to *domum … nidum* (what the birds found: your altars), or as an exclamation of the soul. MS1932 supplies *(Sejam minha casa)* in parentheses; the Hebrew reads 'at your altars' (where the bird nests). The verbless phrase is kept: Portuguese *Os vossos altares* allows both readings, as the Latin does. Nothing supplied.

options.label: Junto aos vossos altares
options.note: Explains the link to the nest; the Hebrew's sense, which the Latin does not state.

decisions.why: 'whose help is from you' (DRB 'whose help is from thee'). *é de vós* is literal but is heard as 'belongs to you'; *vem de* gives *abs* its motion with the plainest verb. MS1932 turns it into hope (*que de ti espera socorro*), which is another sentence.

options.label: é de vós
options.note: Word for word; may be heard as possession.

options.label: está em vós
options.note: Closer to the Hebrew ('whose strength is in you'); loses *abs*.

decisions.why: *ascénsio* is 'an ascent' (L&S cites this very verse under 'a rising'); Greek ἀναβάσεις. The image is of climbs laid out in the heart — the pilgrim going up to the house of v. 2. *Subidas* is the concrete plain word. *Ascensões* keeps the Latin's word but is heard first as the Ascension; DRB paraphrases ('to ascend by steps'); MS1932 *elevações*.

options.label: ascensões
options.note: The cognate; the feast is heard first.

options.label: degraus
options.note: DRB 'by steps'; a supplied image (steps, not ascents).

decisions.why: The Latin echoes *dispósuit … pósuit*, and Portuguese has the same two roots (*dispôs … pôs*). Who 'set' the place is left open by the Latin (the man, or God in the third person; MS1932 glosses *(Deus)*); the bare verb keeps it open. The echo was the draft's first choice, but *que pôs* at the final rhymes with *vem de vós* at the mediant (checks: an accidental rhyme the Latin does not have, a defect under rule 5), and *o lugar que pôs* sounds unfinished. *Estabeleceu* is the plain sense of *pónere* with a place as object (L&S 'to set, appoint'), and keeps the subject as open as the Latin.

options.label: que estabeleceu
options.note: Ruling: the plain sense; the root echo lost to avoid the rhyme.

options.label: que pôs
options.note: The root echo *dispôs … pôs* kept; rhymes with *vós* at the mediant.

decisions.why: The *virtus* row gives *poder* for God's virtus and *vigor* for a man's strength; *Dóminus virtútum* is *Senhor dos poderes* four times in this psalm. Here the pilgrims go 'from strength to strength' (ἐκ δυνάμεως εἰς δύναμιν). Both Vulgate-family witnesses say *virtue* (DRB 'from virtue to virtue', MS1932 *de virtude em virtude*), and the phrase lives in Catholic Portuguese in that form. Latin *virtus* holds strength and excellence at once; Portuguese *virtude* still keeps 'power, efficacy' (*em virtude de*, *a virtude de um remédio*), so it is the one word that holds both, as the Latin does. *De poder em poder* would keep the echo with *Senhor dos poderes* but is heard as a climb in rank; *de força em força* takes *fortitúdo*'s word. Cost, accepted: the echo of *virtútum* inside the psalm is lost unless option `das virtudes` of `virtutum` is taken.

options.label: de virtude em virtude
options.note: Ruling: DRB, MS1932; keeps the Latin's double sense.

options.label: de poder em poder
options.note: The virtus row; echoes *Senhor dos poderes*.

options.label: de força em força
options.note: The sense of the Greek; *força* is fortitúdo's.

decisions.why: Future passive of *vidére* (ὀφθήσεται). *Será visto* keeps the passive and the verb *ver*; MS1932 has the same words. *Aparecerá* is the plain meaning but is *apparére*'s verb (41:3 *aparecerei*). Latin order (verb first) kept: it ends the verse on *Sião*, an oxytone.

decisions.latin: Protéctor noster, áspice, Deus: et réspice in fáciem Christi tui
decisions.why: The glossary foresaw this verse: *áspice* and *réspice* stand side by side and must be decided locally. The rows give both *olhar para*. The Greek splits them: *áspice* here is ἴδε ('see, behold'), *réspice* is ἐπίβλεψον, the verb that 118:132 and 12:3 render *olhai (para)*. So *áspice* takes *vede* (absolute, as the Latin — DRB 'Behold'), and *réspice in* keeps the rows' *olhai para*. *Vede* is safe under rule 3 (the past is *vi*). The vocatives are joined at the head (*Deus, nosso protetor*), natural order (D2); the Latin splits them around the verb. The colon is also the Preces versicle (*Protéctor noster áspice Deus, et réspice in fáciem Christi tui*) and the Introit of Pentecost XIV (with 83:11a).

options.label: Deus, nosso protetor, vede … olhai para
options.note: Ruling: the Greek's two verbs kept apart; natural vocative order.

options.label: Nosso protetor, vede, Deus … olhai para
Deus, nosso protetor, olhai … voltai os olhos para
options.note: Keeps *olhar* for *áspice* (the aspícere row); supplies *os olhos* for the re-.

options.label: Deus, nosso protetor, olhai … olhai para
options.note: Both rows as written; one verb twice where the Latin and Greek have two.

decisions.why: *una* stands after the noun to weigh the number against *míllia*. *Um dia* alone is also 'a day'; *um só dia* (MS1932) keeps the count. *Mélior … super* → *melhor … do que* (the comparative takes *do que*, not the super row's *mais que*, as the *Bonum est … quam* row).

decisions.latin: Elégi abjéctus esse in domo Dei mei
decisions.why: *abjéctus*, from *ab-jácio* 'to throw away, cast down' (L&S; as adjective 'low, mean'); the Greek παραρριπτεῖσθαι is 'to be cast aside'. *Posto de lado* keeps the throwing-aside of both words and the lowly place inside the house. *Abjeto* in Portuguese is moral vileness — a wrong sense. *Desprezado* is the abjéctio row's (21:7 *desprezo*, another Greek word) and puts contempt from others where the Latin has a low place. MS1932 *ser o último* interprets (and DRB 'an abject' is the cognate).

options.label: desprezado
options.note: The abjéctio row's root; contempt rather than a low place.

options.label: rebaixado
options.note: L&S 'cast down to a lower grade'; heard as demoted.

decisions.why: *Elégi … magis quam* is 'I chose … rather than'. *Mais do que* keeps *magis*; *em vez de* is the plain Portuguese of 'rather than' but is another word; MS1932 changes the verb to *Preferi … a morar*.
*bona* (τὰ ἀγαθά), 'good things' (DRB). The *bona tríbuere* row (12:6b) found *bens* heard as property by the blind reader and took *coisas boas*. MS1932 *dos seus bens*.

choices.83:2: Subject first in the second colon (natural order, D2); the Latin puts the two verbs first. *tabernácula → tendas* (row, plural as 42:3). *concupíscere → ansiar por* (row). *átrium → átrio* (row; two blind readers did not know it — kept, the Latin's word). The first colon is sung alone as a responsory and Gradual (Commune C8, Pent05-0, Epi1-0).
choices.83:3: *caro → carne*; *Deus vivus → o Deus vivo* (41:3's words without *forte*). First colon +3: the articles before possessives (rule 5).
choices.83:4: *étenim → pois* (row). *passer → pardal* (row, which names this verse). *turtur → rola* (MS1932). *invénit* perfect → *encontrou*. *ubi ponat* subjunctive → *onde ponha*. Second colon +4: the second *para si* kept (decision `sibi2`).
choices.83:4b: *Rex meus et Deus meus → meu Rei e meu Deus* (formula row, 5:3, 43:5). Second colon −3: the formula; the Latin's *et* is kept.
choices.83:5: *in sǽcula sæculórum → pelos séculos dos séculos* (D27). The second colon is a responsory R. alone (*In sǽcula sæculórum laudábunt te*) and reads alone. Vocative *Senhor* kept at the end of its colon, where the Latin has it. First colon +3: *bem-aventurados* (D19).
choices.83:6: *beátus vir → bem-aventurado o homem* (D19). *auxílium → auxílio*. *in valle lacrimárum → no vale de lágrimas* — the Salve Regina's phrase. The two *in* are both kept (*no vale …, no lugar*). Verb moved before its object (*dispôs no seu coração subidas*), natural order. Length: first colon +4 (*bem-aventurado*, D19's known cost); second colon about −2 against the Latin's 28 syllables.
choices.83:8: *legislátor → legislador* (DRB 'lawgiver', MS1932). *benedictiónem* singular (the Greek has the plural εὐλογίας; the Latin followed). *a bênção*: Portuguese needs an article or *uma*; *a* is lighter. Subject of *ibunt* left unnamed, as the Latin. *Deus deórum → o Deus dos deuses* (D44).
choices.83:9: *exáudi → escutai* (D3); *áuribus pércipe → dai ouvidos* (D4, which names this verse: *dai ouvidos, Deus de Jacó*). *Deus virtútum* follows *Dóminus virtútum* (decision `virtutum`), as 79:8.
choices.83:10: *protéctor → protetor* (row). *Christus → Cristo* (D19; the row names 83:10). Ends with a colon, as the Latin runs on into 83:11 *Quia*.
choices.83:11: The Introit of Pentecost XIV (*… quia mélior est dies una in átriis tuis super mília*) joins 83:10 and 83:11a. *super míllia → do que milhares*.
choices.83:11b: *tabernáculis peccatórum → nas tendas dos pecadores* (the tabernáculum row names this place). *habitáre → habitar*, as 83:5. Second colon −3, accepted.
choices.83:12: Natural order (subject before verb in both colons, D2); the Latin ends each colon on the divine name. *díligere → amar* (row). *misericórdia*, *véritas → verdade* (rows). *grátia → graça*.
choices.83:13: *beátus homo → bem-aventurado o homem*: *homo* and *vir* (83:6) become one word, as in MS1932 and DRB ('the man'); Portuguese has no plain second word (*varão* is archaic). *ambuláre → andar*, *innocéntia → inocência*, *speráre in → esperar em* (rows). Second colon +5: *bem-aventurado* (D19).

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from parallels (no Diurnal Monástico for this psalm). Hard readings: 83:4b verbless *Altária tua*; 83:6 *ascensiónes … in loco, quem pósuit*; 83:8 *de virtúte in virtútem* against D43's *Senhor dos poderes*; 83:10 *áspice / réspice* side by side (the glossary said decide locally); 83:11b *abjéctus*.

Hard checks pass. Soft: 83:6 rhyme *vós / pôs* at mediant and final — fixed (decision `posuit` now rules *que estabeleceu*; the echo *que pôs* kept as option). Length flags accepted (83:3 +3, 83:4 +4, 83:4b −3, 83:5 +3, 83:6 +4, 83:13 +5 — articles, the kept *para si*, *bem-aventurado*; reasons in `choices`).
